evidence: io.lisp:1883-1886: `(unless (= (cdr (assoc :trailer table)) 32) (fnn-refuse "host store trailer is 32 but the model says ~d" ...)) (unless (= (cdr (assoc :header table)) 10) (fnn-refuse ...))`. io.lisp:1859-1860 (fnn-bridge-config-initial): `(when (or (keywordp value) (not (fnn-octet-list-p value))) (fnn-refuse "refused initial group table"))`. This treats a non-octet-list, non-keyword return (malformed) the same as an ACL2 refusal.
fix: Use fnn-fault for the constant mismatch and for a return value that is neither a recognized refusal keyword nor an octet list. Keep fnn-refuse only for ACL2's named refusal.
reviewer: io.lisp:1883-1886 uses fnn-refuse (fnn-store-error, io.lisp:132-133) for a host/model frame-constant mismatch, which is a build defect and should be fnn-fault. io.lisp:1859-1860 handles a malformed non-keyword, non-octet-list return from fn-cfg-host-initial-octets-at the same way as a keyword refusal. Both blur refused and fault, against AGENTS.md. The first is reachable only from a broken image, since the frame grammar fixes the header at 10 and the SHA-256 trailer at 32.
scenario: An image is built with a frame grammar whose trailer or header width differs from the host's hard-coded 32 and 10. Every store open then exits 1, "refused", which callers and tests read as a legitimate policy refusal of the input, when it is a build defect that should exit 4 (fault). In the same way, a malformed return from fn-cfg-host-initial-octets-at is shown to the operator as a refused group table. AGENTS.md requires uncertain, refused, accepted and fault to stay distinct at every boundary.
title: A model/host disagreement or malformed ACL2 result is reported as a refusal (exit 1), not a fault
